_doc: FERNDOWN dating cabinet (#55, Wave F closer, built 2026-07-17-eve; roster #18). Les Wood — Dunhill's master silversmith (from March 1963, 19 years) -> L. & J.S. BRIARS founded 1978 with wife Dolly ('the second ex-Dunhill man to go independent after Sasieni... followed by Ashton-Taylor'). FERNDOWN = the later house-name brand (named for his mansion; UK/US market; 'L. Wood' in Germany). SOURCES: staging/pipedia/Ferndown.json — INCLUDES LES WOOD'S OWN Jan-2020 first-person account (primary!).

history_anchors._doc: Les Wood: Dunhill silver-mounting dept from March 1963 (under Jack Spriggs, took over after ~2 years). 1978: asked to buy the machinery and set up outside -> L. & J.S. BRIARS with Dolly (ex-Dunhill finisher — her double-oiling finish story = the house oil-cure); kept mounting DUNHILL'S pipes as a contractor until 1980/81. Early pipes sold as L.&J.S BRIARS / ELLWOOD / LES WOOD / L. WOOD (trademark vagaries); later ~1500-2000/yr as FERNDOWN (UK/US) + 'L. Wood' (Germany). Ferndown-name start = NOT dated in source -> approx floor. Oil-cured Italian+Spanish plateau; hand-cut stems; THE SILVER = the signature (bands/caps/spigots/army mounts on nearly all; LJS engraved on the mount). Grades by FINISH: BARK (~90%, dark rusticated), ANTIQUE BARK (tan), REO (brown/red smooth), ROOT (orange smooth), TUDOR ROOT (orange-brown) + SIZE STARS (1-4) + SG = straight grain. Sandblasted 'Premier Sandblast' pieces = blasted in CANADA (Maxim Engel arrangement, pipes2smoke era) — distinct from Dolly's hand-cut bark rustication. Wood's metalwork also served Ashton, Comoy's, Bentley (John Aylesbury POY 2008). 2020: semi-retired, limited production ('57 years in the trade' = counting from 1963).

brand_marks.physical: Silver-mounted almost throughout (rings/ferrules for spigots); LJS engraved on mounts; finish-name grades + 1-4 stars; 90% = Bark rustication (Dolly's two-point drill work).

line_years._notes: Finish grades (Bark/Reo/Root/Tudor Root) span the brand -> unencoded. Premier Sandblast = Canada-blasted late-era pieces (undated edges).
